objective: Replace frequent discounting with simpler everyday, month-long and best-price tiers.
businessContext: The retailer sought to shift from a promotion-led department-store model to simpler pricing and a specialty-store presentation.
strategy: Remove most promotional activity and teach customers a new value system through a brand and pricing reset.
outcomes: JCPenney reported a 25.2% comparable-store-sales decline in 2012.
The company later said the prior strategy did not resonate and returned most of the business to a promotional model.
whatWorked: The proposition attempted to reduce complexity.
whatFailed: It removed familiar deal signals faster than customer reference prices and shopping habits could change.
Multiple simultaneous changes made diagnosis and recovery harder.
transferConditions: Use when testing changes to established promotional expectations and price architecture.
nonTransferConditions: Do not assume simpler pricing is automatically more persuasive to promotion-trained customers.
